entries.german: XII. Herzog Heinrich I. von Schlesien gestattet den Kolonisten* des Vincenz-Klosters zu Breslau ,in Polsnitz Deutsches Recht. 1228. Aus dem Originale. In nomine patris et filii et spiritus sancti. Notum sit omnibus, quod ego, Henricus, dei gracia dux Zlesie, ad peticionem Alberti '), abbatis sancti Vin- cencii in Vratizlavia et fratrum ejus, concessimus 2) jus Teutonicale hospitibus eorum, manentibus in Polsnicia 3), ut sint inmunes ab angariis, que fieri soient Polonis secundum consuetudinem terre, que vulgo dici soient povoz, prevod, slad, preseka, et a solutionibus, que soient exigi, sieut est strosa, podvorove et his similia, eo tarnen pacto interveniente, ut de quolibet manso, qui solvit abbati, percipiamus duas mensuras, unam tritici et aliam avene, quas mensuras ipsi in Lesniciam4), ad curiam ducis ducent. Ad castrum edificandum pro magna necessitate juvabunt. Ad expedicionem ibunt sicut aliiTeutonici. Graves causas nos judicabimus, scilicet capitales, per nos vel per alium baronern no strum. Sivero inter hominem predicte ville et inter hominem ville alteriusdorainii altercacio fuerit, coram nobis vel coram castellano, in cujus castellatura fuerit, litigare debebunt. Alias appellationes judicet scultetus, satisfaciens conque- rentibus, quod si injuste judicaverit, coram nobis respondeat. Ne quis vero ausu temerario hanc nostre constitucionis libertatem infringere présumât, pre- senti pagine sigilli nostri munimine (sic!) appendimus. Factum anno millesimo ducentésimo vicésimo octavo. aufser Zarzisk, auch Hartwigowicze, (Jastrzygowitz? N.N. O. 2 M. von Rosenberg) Koscze- liske, (Koselwitz, N. *j M. von Rosenberg), Lgota, (S. O. an Zarzisk grunzend) und beide Borki, (Grofs- und Klein-Borek, О. 1 M. von Rosenberg) mit demselben Rechte, wie andere Güter des Klosters in anderen Herzogthümern, zu besitzen. *) War Abt vom J. 1214 bis 1248. 3) ego — concessimus. 3) Polsnitz, S. O. S. 2% M. von Neumarkt. 4) Lissa, 2 M. von Polsnitz. Ebendahin amisten die Bauern von Sablath das Herzogskorn fahren. Urkundenb. No. 19. S7 290 Urkundenbuch.
entries.english:
Henry I, Duke of Silesia, grants the settlers of the Monastery of St. Vincent in Breslau German law at Polsnitz. 1228. From the original.

In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Let it be known to all that I, Henry, by the grace of God Duke of Silesia, at the request of Albert, abbot of St. Vincent in Breslau, and his brethren, have granted German law to their settlers residing at Polsnitz, so that they shall be exempt from the compulsory services customarily imposed on Poles according to the custom of the land, commonly called povoz, prevod, slad, and preseka, and from the payments customarily exacted, such as strosa, podvorove, and the like. On this condition, however: from each mansus that pays the abbot, we shall receive two measures, one of wheat and the other of oats, which the settlers shall carry to Lesnica, to the duke’s court. In a great emergency they shall help build a castle. They shall go on military expeditions like the other Germans. We shall judge serious cases, namely capital cases, either ourselves or through another of our barons. If a dispute arises between a man of the aforesaid village and a man of a village belonging to another lord, they shall litigate before us or before the castellan in whose castellany it lies. The scultetus shall judge other appeals, giving satisfaction to the complainants; if he has judged unjustly, he shall answer before us. Lest anyone presume with reckless audacity to infringe this liberty established by us, we have attached our seal as confirmation to this document. Done in the year 1228.

In addition to Zarzisk, the monastery is also to possess Hartwigowicze, Koscze-liske, Lgota, and both Borki, with the same right as its other properties in other duchies. Hartwigowicze is identified in the source as Jastrzygowitz (uncertain), northeast of Rosenberg; Koscze-liske as Koselwitz, northeast of Rosenberg; Lgota borders Zarzisk to the southeast; and the two Borki are Groß- and Klein-Borek, one mile east of Rosenberg.

Notes: Albert was abbot from 1214 to 1248. Polsnitz lies southeast of Neumarkt, two and a half miles away. Lesnica is two miles from Polsnitz; the peasants of Sablath also carried the duke’s grain there. See charter no. 19.
